data.title: Anime Review: Yomi no Tsugai (Daemons of the Shadow Realm)
data.incipit: Hiromu Arakawa is one of the legendary mangakas of our time. If you don’t know, she did Fullmetal Alchemist, Silver Spoon, and The Heroic Legend of Arslan... all of which received anime adaptations. Now, her...
data.body: Hiromu Arakawa is one of the legendary mangakas of our time. If you don’t know, she did Fullmetal Alchemist, Silver Spoon, and The Heroic Legend of Arslan... all of which received anime adaptations. Now, her latest series has been no different. This is Yomi no Tsugai (Daemons of the Shadow Realm). Enough of the intro... Let’s Jam The Story Yuru is a boy working in a village all for the sake of his sister Asa, who, for some reason, is kept inside a cell with only a select few allowed to see her. Along for the ride is Yuru’s friend Danji, an energetic boy who doesn’t seem to be exceptional in anything that he does. As Yuru is killing a pheasant for dinner, he looks up at a pair of chemtrails, thinking that it’s a dragon flying overhead. When he returns, a brilliant flash lights up the sky, and suddenly, the barrier protecting the village disappears. Military men storm the village, killing anyone and everything in their path as dual helicopters circle overhead, providing air support. Then, a girl in a red trench coat shows up and mutters “Gobble” over and over again as people’s bodies are sliced in half effortlessly. Yuru’s grandmother knows that they are here for him and puts out the order to find and hide him, but it’s too late. A traveling merchant by the name of Dera is more than he seems. Once he sees the village getting attacked, he pulls out a cellphone and reports in on the situation. He storms the village, taking out as many soldiers as he can until he catches up with Yuru. The grandmother instructs Dera to take him away and go into hiding. He obliges, but they run into a bit of an issue. He gives Yuru an amulet depicting the twin statues at the village’s front gates and tells him to slot it into the hole between them. When he does so, two yellow sentient pieces of energy rip apart the helicopters, later manifesting into a man and woman named Migi and Hidari (Right and Left). They are Yuru’s Daemons! After the attack, Dera and Hana bring Yuru down the mountain and introduce him to the real world, which is a massive culture shock for him. Almost straight out of the gate, Yuru becomes hunted by members of the Kagemori Clan. He winds up getting captured, only to discover that his real sister, Asa, is staying with them. Confused, Asa offers him an explanation, but it’s very hard for him to conceive that the Asa he visited back in the village was a fake all along. The Kagemoris have an interest in Yuru because he is the one prophesied to acquire the power of Seal, the other half of Asa’s Break; however, Dera tracks Yuru down and brings him back under his protection. Throughout it all, Yuru must track down information on his missing parents while unraveling the mystery of the various clans out there trying to capture him and Asa to acquire their powers. All the while, the Higashi Clan and Kagemori Clan have to deal with their own internal problems as not all clans get along with their own members. Characters Yuru Yuru is our main protagonist, and even though he hasn’t awakened it yet, he is the one who is compatible with the power of Seal, one of the two legendary Daemons. His entire life was spent in Higashi village, isolated from the modern world. Because of this, he only knows primitive skills such as hunting for his own food and surviving off the land. His mindset is noble, though, as he is very loyal to his village and to his friends. He would do anything to protect them, but he’s not a pushover by any means. His father always taught him to kill or be killed, and this is accentuated when he’s attacked by bandits and has to fend for his life. He recites the lessons his father told him before he and his mother took the real Asa and left the mountain, leaving him all by himself. This creates his rough and gruff attitude while maintaining a kind heart because he understands the value of friends and family. He has an indirect comedic side when he’s introduced to the real world, as he has no clue about anything. He’s shocked he can buy meat at a store, doesn’t know what a phone is, and is even marveled that something as simple as aspirin is produced en masse and readily available. He’s a very balanced character! Asa The one we met in the village was a doppelganger; however, the real Asa has one of the biggest brother complexes you will ever see. You would swear that she’s in love with Yuru; however, there is a moment during the show where she dreams of a normal life... which includes getting a boyfriend, so that throws that theory straight out of the window. Still, she obsesses over every little thing about Yuru, from the way he looks, to the sound of his voice, to the mere fact that he smiles at her, or even agrees to talk to her... she acts like it’s the biggest event in the world. Outside of this, she’s very complex emotionally. After she was killed and forced to awaken Break, she has come to regret her isolated life, but she understands it’s for her own protection. Her dream is just to live a normal life with Yuru and her parents, but the fact that she can’t frustrates her. Still, she’s grateful to the Kagemori Clan for taking her in and protecting her, so she swears to use the power of Break to protect them, as it’s the least she can do to show that gratitude. She can be quite annoying whenever Yuru’s around, but when she gets down and dirty, she is quite the force to be reckoned with... even if she can’t fully control Break just yet. Hidari and Migi Otherwise known as Right and Left, they are the Daemons that were encased in statues overseeing and protecting Higashi Village. Upon his escape with Dera, Yuru isn’t given much information, but is told to forge a contract with them by offering the statues his blood. He does so, and they come to life. Apparently, they see Yuru as a kind master, and love the fact that Yuru will let them do as they please without much restriction. They are hard-headed, love to fight, and aren’t afraid of anything... mainly because their bodies are made of stone! They are excellent supporting characters for Yuru, who not only protect him, but also keep him in check from time to time as good guardians should! Dera Dera starts off as a traveling merchant who visits Higashi village. Whenever he shows up, everyone is happy to see him, but that’s just a cover. His real mission is to watch over Yuru as a member of the Higashi Clan. When the village is attacked by the Kagemori Clan, he’s the one who helps Yuru escape and becomes his guardian in the real world. He’s also the one who helps form a kind of ceasefire pact with the Kagemori Clan and even enlists their help and vice versa from time to time as the Kagemori Clan deals with unrest from within their ranks. Outside of being Yuru’s protector, he’s kind of a carefree goofball that doesn’t mind abusing Jin’s invitation to drink at his bar, or losing all of his money gambling on horse races. Despite his goofiness, when it comes to protecting Yuru, he is a top-notch combatant that knows how to use his head! Hana She is Dera’s partner in crime and also a member of the Higashi Clan. Known as Gravedigger, she is usually summoned to clean up some of the Higashi’s Clan’s “messes” by disposing of their bodies. Because she knows the Higashi Clan also wants Break and Seal for themselves, she feigns ignorance when it comes to Yuru and Dera’s whereabouts, despite the fact that they are all living together in a hideout. She’s very short-tempered, finds kids highly annoying, and is constantly scolding Dera for squandering their savings on stupid stuff... especially when Dera ignores a lot of requests from the Higashi Clan, thus not earning any income. Despite her transgressions, she does have a heart, and though it is to her chagrin, she takes in Yuru... and others... along the way. I can only see her as a comic relief type character, but there are some moments where she does play a bigger role. The fact that she is deceiving her own clan is rather odd, as it doesn’t really benefit her all that much, but she still does it for Yuru’s sake, if that tells you anything about the true nature of her character. The Kagemori Clan There are still a TON of characters to go, and some of these will dig a bit too deep into spoiler territory, so I’m going to lump them all together. Gonzo Kagemori is the head of the clan, and he is about as kind as he is ruthless. He has a heart of gold and has zero problems taking strangers in and protecting them. In fact, a lot of the members of the Kagemori Clan are either orphans or people he came across who were down on their luck and needed a helping hand. His demons have the power to force other demons to coexist with one another, so he can make contracts with as many demons as he likes... which makes him terrifyingly powerful... almost at a legendary status amongst the clans. Just the mention of his name sends chills down anyone’s spine because of this. He’s always happy, smiling, and very carefree... until you cross the clan... then, he is anything but. Friend, Family Member, Foe, or otherwise, he doesn’t care. The moment you attack the clan or betray them, it is an instant death sentence for you, showing his ruthless and cold side. If I’m being honest... he is my favorite character in the show. He shows that the Kagemori Clan isn’t truly as evil as it seems, but because of his power and influence, it’s also a clan not to be taken lightly. His loyalty to his members is unmatched, but his punishment for those who betray that loyalty is something to be feared. It’s the perfect yin/yang combination, and there’s just something about him that just makes me love him as a character. We have Jin Kagemori, one of Gonzo’s sons. Like Hana, he is the Kagemori Clan’s cleaner. He is very calm and mild-mannered, but he is also very apologetic and respectful when he knows there have been wrongs that need to be righted. Despite being from a different clan, and although he was a bit apprehensive at first, he works with Dera for the sake of the Kagemori Clan, showing that he is also analytical and calculated. Above all else, you can tell he is loyal and trustworthy, but he also carries out Gonzo’s wishes without fail because he understands what it means to be for the Clan. If Gonzo suddenly wanted Dera killed, Jin would be the type of person to apologize to Dera for disposing of him. He is my second favorite character in the show! Asuma is another one of Gonzo’s sons, but he seems the least trustworthy, and that’s because it’s his running gag. He doesn’t know how to smile properly, and because of that, he comes off as sly or scheming whenever he says anything. Many think he doesn’t mean what he says, or he’s just a snake, but the truth is, he does mean everything he says; he cares deeply and is also very loyal to the clan. Next we have Akio and Haruo Kuroya, as well as Gabby. All of them are orphans taken in by the Kagemori Clan. While Akio and Haruo would go into spoilers, Gabby ends up befriending Asa to the point where she would do anything to protect her. Yes, she looks like a female Edward Elric, but she is a light tsundere character. She’s a firecracker when she wants to be, but she’s caring... especially with Asa. She’s tired of Asa always apologizing for things, so she literally kicks her rear whenever she does. She seemed very evil at first during the Higashi Village attack, but she’s just another misunderstood character. Hikaru Kagemori is another one of Gonzo’s sons and is a pacifist. He wants to make manga and even teaches Asa how to draw to be one of his assistants. He doesn’t agree with his father’s ruthlessness, and typically doesn’t involve himself in the family’s affairs. He just wants peace and quiet, but his demons can repair the manor whenever it’s damaged, so he’s quite useful in that regard because... yeah... the place gets torn up A LOT in this series. Danji We also have Danji... a super minor character at first who turns out to have a very significant role later. I’ll just say he’s Yuru’s best friend. Shingo & Ivan The last ones I’ll touch on are Shingo and Ivan. Shingo is a man whose greed knows no bounds (where have we heard this before?). He wants to acquire Break and Seal for himself, and is one of the people causing problems for the Kagemori Clan. Ivan is a hired mercenary who works under Shingo and is probably one of the most interesting characters in the series. He is a seriously skilled combatant with twin demon katanas... and to show off his power, he 1 v 4’s Yuru, Migi, Hidari, and Dera at the same time... and survives. He is set up to be one of the series’ main antagonists, and I just love his composure during battle plus his overall attitude. Needless to say, he’s my third favorite character! Yes, as much as I have spent here on the characters, there are still a TON of characters I didn’t mention, like Sakurazawa, the Kagemori Clan’s doctor, Yama the Shaman, Iori Shingo, Ken Tadera, Granny Yamaha, and all of the different demons throughout the world. There is such a MASSIVE cast here to cover, but hopefully, I covered all the main and important ones. Art, Animation, and Sound Come on, guys... It’s bones. We already know it’s going to be good... and my God, is it good. Despite having a massive cast of characters, every single one of them looked unique, distinct, and had their personalities shine through in their designs. From facial expressions to clothing, when you saw a character, you not only recognized who they were, but you already understood the type of character they would be. When you saw Jin, you knew he would be calm and collected, but someone not to mess with. When you saw Shingo, you knew he was crazed and eccentric. When you saw Asa, you... okay... nothing could prepare you for the brother complex, but still... her design matches just how badass she is on the battlefield. The world itself was very well-crafted. From the stark differences of Higashi Village to the Modern World, nothing felt out of place. Even with Higashi Village being stuck in the 1800s (or so), it still felt like a natural part of the world because of it being isolated in the mountains; its location made it believable that they would be cut off from everything, making Yuru’s confusion about modern technology and convenience valid. As far as the animation goes, it was also great. Every fight in this series absorbed you into the action, drew you into every movement, spell, and special effect. Then again, as I said, this is bones we’re talking about here... they know how to deliver, and boy did they deliver. Even simple effects like a demon materializing looked so fluid and well pulled off. Most shows would have a PNG just fade in with an effect, but not here. These demons were fading in mid-animation... whether it’s riding on a magical horse or simply just walking. The level of detail and effort put in here was just top-notch. Plus, the Ivan fight versus Left, Right, Yuru, and Dera was insane. They truly pulled off how skilled Ivan is, and it truly made you believe that this guy could be unkillable just from the animation alone. That’s not easy to do. As for sound? The show’s soundtrack stood out well. It’s one of those that had excellent music to draw you into the action scenes, dark and brooding music during moments of drama, and then it had corny music during the comedic parts. Every part of the soundtrack was composed with the intention to get the most out of every scene. Vaundy, which did a banger for The Summer Hikaru Died, was back for the first opening with Tobu Toki, and I thought it was the stronger of the two. That’s another thing... this show was 24 episodes long, and starting with Episode 13, we received a new opening for the show. Remember the times when anime would air for much longer than 12 or 13 episodes, and we always looked forward to the new opening? Yeah... that brought me back to when we swapped over to back shot by Masanori Otoda. While that song was good in its own right, I still preferred Vaundy’s opening instead. Still, you can’t go wrong with either one, though. Overall Thoughts I don’t know what to say other than... It’s Hiromu Arakawa. This is the fourth work of hers in a row to get adapted into an anime. The previous ones were Fullmetal Alchemist, Silver Spoon, and The Legend of Arslan... and the fact that she gets anime adaptations isn’t a fluke... It’s because she knows how to make an amazing story with character depth that stands the test of time. Arakawa is just a master at creating characters, and despite Daemons of the Shadow Realm having one of her biggest casts ever, you still feel the depth of her characters here. Even supporting characters have tremendous depth and have a usefulness in the story. She makes you care about them as much as the story and world itself, and that is very, VERY hard to do consistently across multiple series, and yet, she pulls it off every single time. As I said above, the story is engaging, the fights are amazing, bones brought her work to life in ways that only they can, the music drove home every moment, and everything felt as cohesive as ever. The ONLY complaint that I would have is that the series ended on a cliffhanger without a definitive conclusion, but that can be forgiven because as soon as the final episode aired, it was announced that Daemons of the Shadow Realm was receiving a second season, so we’re not done yet! I am not sure if Season 2 will also have 24 episodes, but with how much I enjoyed this show, I sure hope that it does! Whether you have seen any of Arakawa’s previous works or not, if you just want an amazing shonen battle anime to sink your teeth into with actual depth in its story and characters, then you cannot go wrong with Daemons of the Shadow Realm. Simply put... watch this show! Overall Score: 4.5 / 5 Daemons of the Shadow Realm Daemons of the Shadow Realm is the latest work from Hiromu Arakawa about a boy named Yuru who has only known an isolated life in a small village. After an attack, he escapes the mountain and must face the modern world, find his lost parents, and avoid being hunted by clans who want his unawakened power... all while learning to deal with the Daemons and their masters. Pros Great story In-depth characters Thrilling action Excellent animation and effects Cons I can’t really think of many flaws outside of the comedy being a little too over-the-top at times. Overall 4.5

data.title: I Love Justin Hartley’s Comments On Jensen Ackles’ Tracker Season 4 Return, But What About Melissa Roxburgh?
data.incipit: (Image credit: Darko Sikman/CBS, Darko Sikman/CBS, Sergei Bachlakov/CBS) Tracker is gearing up for Season 4 amid the 2026 TV schedule, and there is much to be excited about. For one, Jensen Ackles will...
data.body: (Image credit: Darko Sikman/CBS, Darko Sikman/CBS, Sergei Bachlakov/CBS) Tracker is gearing up for Season 4 amid the 2026 TV schedule , and there is much to be excited about. For one, Jensen Ackles will once again be returning as Russell Shaw, the brother of Justin Hartley 's Colter, after taking on some shady work to protect him. Hartley shared what’s in store for Ackles’ return, and, as pumped as I am, I’m still wondering where Melissa Roxburgh stands and whether she'll return as Colter and Russell's sister, Dory. What Justin Hartley Said About Jensen Ackles’ Return Ackles made his first appearance as Colter’s estranged brother in the first season. Since then, the two have slowly repaired their relationship while learning more about their late father. The two siblings even worked on some cases together (with varied results). Despite his busy schedule and working on The Boys prequel, Vought Rising , Ackles will indeed be back for Season 4. Not only that, but he’ll be appearing early in the season, as Hartley confirmed to TV Insider : Well, right now he is about probably 100 meters away from me. He’s in at least one [episode], and we’ll have him back when we can. I think probably in the new year, we’ll have him back for a few. I love that even though Ackles is so busy with other projects, he’s still trying to come back to Tracker when he can, and the producers are making sure that happens. It’s been fun to see Colter and Russell’s dynamic, especially since Hartley and Ackles are longtime pals . Knowing that Ackles might even be back for the latter half of Season 4 is making me curious as to what could be in store. As for this first appearance in the upcoming season, Russell is going to be reaching out for his brother’s help. Hartley explained: What’s he been up to is he won’t tell me. Well, he kind of can’t, right? I mean, there’s a quid pro quo thing that happened at the end of Season 3, and he’s like, ‘As long as my brother doesn’t find out about this, I’ll do this thing for you.' But when we find him and when he reaches out to Colter, he needs help with something. One of his buddies is in dire straits, big time dire straits — and not a self-inflicted thing, just sort of something that happened to him, and he thinks of his brother Colter, and he’s like, ‘I bet you Colter can help you with this.’ So, he reaches out and of course Colter’s willing to help and it reunites the two brothers and they go on this pretty epic journey. Even though Russell is clearly keeping something from Colter, I like that he still feels the need to reach out for help. It's hard to predict what will happen when the Shaw brothers get together, and I can only assume that whatever Russell is hiding will eventually come to light. For now, though, their relationship seems to be unchanged. The more they get together, though, the more I wonder about their sister. What's Going On With Melissa Roxburgh? Roxburgh guest starred in Tracker ’s first season as Colter and Russell’s sister, Dr. Dory Shaw. So far, that’s been her only appearance. Of course, Roxburgh was busy with her show, The Hunting Party , which was unfortunately canceled after two seasons on NBC . Now that her schedule is a bit more open, could we be seeing Dory in the near-future? Hartley weighed in on the possibility, and he’s keeping an open mind: It’s possible. All these people that I thought, what a great idea to have on the show, they’re all so damn busy now, right? It’s not a secret that they’re all really good, so they’re all working a lot. So, anything’s possible. We’ll see. Ever since Season 1, I have wanted nothing more than to have all three Shaw siblings on screen together. As for how the show could bring back Dory, I’m not sure. I think the logical route would be to bring her into a story involving the trio's dad, and perhaps that could connect to what Russell is hiding from Colter. As of now, Roxburgh doesn't seem to be attached to any projects since The Hunting Party , but it’s possible she’s still working on something that's just yet to it be announced. I'll certainly maintain optimism about Melissa Roxburgh returning to Tracker . But, for now, I'll just be grateful that Justin Hartley and Jensen Ackles will get to share the screen more. Check out Season 4, which premieres on Sunday, October 4 at 9:30 p.m. ET on CBS. The show will then move to its regular time slot of 9 p.m. ET the following week. Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News Passionate writer. Obsessed with anything and everything entertainment, specifically movies and television. Can get easily attached to fictional characters.
